the effects of RPs on the differentiation of photoreceptor cells.
the development of a new co-culture method that could improve the expression of photoretinal cells in the differentiation protocol of hESC.
the differentiation of retinal pigment epithelia and progenitor cells derived human embryonic stems cells.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
RPE cells can be used to improve differentiation of photoreceptors from RPCs.
the co-culture with RPE cells through cell-to-cell contact is more effective in induction of photoreceptor-specific marker than the use of insert.
the co-culture system with direct contact of RPE cells and RPCs is superior to the co-culture with insert for induction of photoreceptor cells.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the direct co-culture of RP cells with RPE sheet is the most effective model for the generation of retinal cells.
RPE cells can induce photoreceptor differentiation from RPCs and the cell-to-cell interaction is more efficient in compare with the indirect co-culture method.
RPE cells are able to induce RPCs to differentiate into mature photoreceptors and the use of insert could be used to induce photoreceptor differentiation.
The main takeaway from our work is that
RPE cells are capable to direct the RPCs differentiation to mature photoreceptors and this effect can be improved by the direct co-culture.
co-culture of hESC with RPE sheet can be a good tool to differentiate RPCs into photoreceptor cells.
